questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How zoos look after pandas
Why some animals have black-and-white colouring
How animals see colours
Why peacocks and frogs are so colourful
questions.why: Becca says hundreds of species are black and white, and they try to find out why.

questions.q: What is Neil's first guess about why animals are black and white?
options: To attract a partner
To keep cool in the sun
To look like other animals
It has something to do with survival
questions.why: Neil says he's not sure, but 'probably something about survival'.

questions.q: What do some scientists think zebras' stripes do?
options: Stop flies and other insects from biting
Help zebras find each other in long grass
Keep zebras warm during cold nights
Make zebras look bigger to lions
questions.why: Neil says some scientists think the stripes prevent bites from flies and other insects.

questions.q: How did zoologist Dr Martin How test this idea?
options: He painted stripes on insects
He watched zebras in the wild for a year
He covered horses in rugs with different patterns
He compared zebras with pandas
questions.why: He tested it by covering horses in stripes, trying different patterns of rugs.

options: Only very thin stripes worked against flies
Flies preferred black-and-white patterns
Brightly coloured patterns worked best
Almost any black-and-white pattern stopped flies
questions.why: He says practically every high-contrast black and white pattern was really effective at stopping flies.

questions.q: According to Becca, why is black and white useful for giant pandas?
options: It helps them stand out clearly on green grass
It hides them from far away in snowy forests
It warns other animals to stay away from them
It protects their skin from the strong sun
questions.why: She says seen from a distance in snowy mountain forests, black and white is the perfect disguise.

questions.q: Why does Professor Tim Caro talk about his 15 photos of pandas?
options: To show that pandas are hard to photograph in zoos
To show that pandas are shy and hide from people
Missing a panda in them showed him they're hidden
Because the photos won an important prize
questions.why: In two photos he saw only rocks and snow, then realised a panda was there, and it clicked.

questions.q: What is Hannah Rowland's view about why penguins are black and white?
options: There's usually a mix of reasons, not just one
It is only for camouflage when in the water
Scientists have now found one clear reason
It mainly helps them keep warm on the ice
questions.why: She says science never has a black-and-white answer; it's often 'a very complex mixture of reasons'.
